Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed by the latency and cost controls. We're looking at consolidating our current quarterly purchases into a single annual commitment to simplify forecasting. A couple of specific asks: 

- Can Redwood offer a stepwise discount schedule tied to committed annual token buckets?
- If we convert our current quarterly uplift pattern into an annualized commit, how would monthly true-ups and credits for unused capacity work?
- Are you able to co-term the new annual commitment with our existing contract (ends 2027-06-30)?

I attached our Q3 usage export to give you a sense of run-rate. Procurement and I would like a ballpark pricing example (two tranches: base + growth) and any required changes to the SOW or billing.

Appreciate a quick sketch so we can review internally.

Hi Sara — thanks for the usage export, that helps. Quick response while we pull numbers:

1) Stepwise discounts: yes — we typically model a tiered discount by committed annual tokens. Example approach: 
   - Tranche A (0 - 3M tokens): standard list price with 8-12% commit discount
   - Tranche B (3M - 10M): incremental discount 5-9% depending on term and payment cadence
   - Tranche C (10M+): custom pricing / executive approval

2) Billing & true-ups: we can do monthly consumption reporting with monthly true-ups against the annual committed amount. Unused committed tokens are handled via a credit pool applied to future invoices within the contract year (we do not auto-refund unless negotiated). If you expect consistent growth, we can structure scheduled uplift points to reduce unused-credit friction.

3) Co-term: co-terming is possible; it usually requires an amendment to the current MSA and we can align the new annual commitment to end 2027-06-30.

I'll ask Ben to sketch a concrete two-tranche example (numbers + estimated discount) and Monica will confirm billing language. Expect an internal note from us by EOD tomorrow.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Sara — looping in a quick example based on the Q3 export and the growth signals you shared:

Proposal (annualized): 12-month term, annual commitment broken into two tranches:
- Tranche 1: 4,000,000 tokens (base commit) — list = $0.0006/token, commit discount = 12% -> $0.000528/token
- Tranche 2: 6,000,000 tokens (growth buffer) — list = $0.0006/token, commit discount = 7% -> $0.000558/token

Estimated blended rate = $0.000545/token (if both tranches purchased). If you convert current quarterly purchases into this structure and sign the annual commit we can offer: 
- One-time onboarding credit of $5,000 applied to first invoice (for SSO/workshop)
- Up to 30% of unused committed tokens can be converted to a one-time rollover credit into Q1 of next year (requires explicit clause in SOW)

Notes on billing: monthly invoices with true-ups; if you exceed committed monthly quantity we bill overage at list price unless you want overage at a reduced step price (we can add that to the SOW).

If this aligns, I'll prepare a redlined SOW + pricing exhibit and Monica can route for approvals.

-Ben

- If we uplift mid-contract (e.g., add another 2M tokens in month 6), do we get retroactive access to the tranche discount for those newly-committed tokens or do they bill at overage rates until the next true-up?

Procurement has asked us to attach a PO template to confirm timing/PO language — attaching. Also, we prefer credits applied on the next invoice automatically rather than manual redemption — is that doable?

Hi Sara — quick clarifications: 

- The 30% rollover cap is applied to the annual committed pool (blended) unless you want us to carve it by tranche; carve-outs add administrative overhead but are possible.
- Uplifts mid-contract: standard behavior is that newly-committed tokens are priced at list/overage until the next monthly true-up where we reconcile and apply the tranche pricing retroactively for the billing month in which the uplift was committed. If you prefer immediate tranche pricing on mid-contract uplifts we can add a provision in the SOW that re-prices the uplifted quantity as of the uplift date (this requires approval from finance and may affect the discount depth).

Attached is a short amortization example that shows monthly invoicing + true-up math and how credits flow if a tranche is underused. Let us know if you want the same in your PO format and we'll merge it.

Thanks,
Monica
